chapters.title: Chapter 401: Ademary Awakened Bureau [1]
paragraphs: "Whoa... So cool!" Darian whispered in awe as he looked around the bustling hall, his eyes wide as he took in the sleek modern architecture and the fully geared Hunters walking back and forth. Pure admiration wrote itself across his face.
Standing beside him, Soren caught sight of Ryan smiling and subtly shaking his head. He raised a brow in silent inquiry.
Noticing his look, Ryan rubbed the back of his neck with an awkward smile. "Ah, it’s just... I was pretty much like this when I first visited the Bureau back then too."
"I see... Well, now that I remember, I was surprised a lot too."

Though he hadn’t shown it quite as outwardly as they had, the initial feeling of stepping into the heart of the Hunter world was undeniable. And considering Darian’s age and lively personality, a reaction like this was practically a given.
"Darian, let’s go. You can tour the bureau later," Soren called out. "I will accompany you myself."
"Ah, ok!" Darian snapped out of his daze and hurriedly followed after them.
They went straight to the reception but had to wait in line for ten or so minutes before their turn came.
"Good morning, how can I help you?" the receptionist asked, her tone professional but friendly.
"I’m here to have someone take an awakening test," Soren replied, gesturing toward Darian.
The receptionist nodded and pulled up a form on her terminal. "Name of the applicant?"
"Darian Dervish."
She typed it in, then slid a small tablet across the counter. "Please fill out these forms and pay the test fee."
Soren paid the fee while Darian filled out the forms with Ryan’s help. Once everything was processed, the receptionist handed them a small card.
"Take this to Building C, just outside the main hall and to the left. Someone there will guide you through the rest of the process."

They thanked her and headed outside, following the directions to a smaller building connected to the main hall by a covered walkway. The door slid open as they approached, revealing a waiting room with a few other applicants and a staff member behind a desk.
Soren told them to wait and walked over to the staff member behind the desk. After a brief conversation, he returned.
"Our turn should come in about half an hour. Let’s sit down and wait.
Ryan and Darian nodded and found seats in the waiting area. While Darian and Ryan looked around the room, Soren activated Eyes of Truth and started inspecting everyone in the vicinity.

Most of the applicants were older than Darian and Ryan, around eighteen or nineteen, and dressed well enough to make it obvious they came from wealthy families. Unfortunately, his ability revealed that most lacked the aptitude needed to awaken; only two had a genuine chance, with 4th- and 5th-Circle potential, respectively.

Among the crowd, however, a pair of twin sisters around Darian’s age soon drew his attention. Wearing luxurious dresses that marked them as high nobility, they sat with refined composure that seemed far beyond their age. What truly set them apart was their potential, which soared at the rare eighth circle, matching Darian’s, along with an impressive array of unique traits and talents.
’I wonder if this is their first time taking the test...’ He mused calmly, until a sudden prickle of pressure broke through his thoughts.

He instinctively turned toward the source of the gaze and met a pair of piercing purple eyes. The woman beside the twins watched him intently, her posture settling into a subtle, guarded stance. Soren gave a faint smile, then casually looked away, breaking eye contact.
She stared at him for a few moments longer, measuring his calm demeanor, before finally turning her attention back to the twins.
Soren knew why she was vigilant. Apart from her, he was the strongest person in the room, making it natural for her to single him out.
A swift glance through Eyes of Truth brought up her status screen.
Name: Shabnam Mahren
Race: Human
Age: 35
Status: Healthy
Rank: 6th Circle (Mid Stage)
Current Mana Level: 2,140,079
Mental State: Cautious, Curious, Watchful
Abilities: Amethyst Thunder Constitution (SS-Rank), Papilion’s Veil (A-Rank)
Affinities: Lightning (Grade 8 - SS Rank), Water (Grade 5 - C Rank)
Hidden Talent / Traits: Overprotective, Independent Streak, Lightning’s Favor
Potential: 8th Circle (Estimated)
Investment Value: SUPREME

’Oh, she’s really good.’ Soren thought as he studied her profile. Since she was older than Zura or Zoe, he guessed she hadn’t focused as much on her own cultivation as they had, or perhaps awakened late like him. That would explain why she was only at the 6th circle. But then again, having a 6th circle cultivation was still impressive no matter the age; it just depended on the perspective.
He took another quick glance at them and nodded inwardly.

Their hair and eye colors differed, but the twins’ features subtly resembled the woman’s. And given their shared surname and her overprotective trait, the woman was probably their mother or a close relative.
"Layan, Lamya, let’s go. It’s your turn."
He heard the woman speak and watched as the twins stood up in unison, adjusting their dresses before following her.
"Huh?" Darian muttered beside him, his eyes widening as he stared after the trio.
Soren glanced at him. "What’s wrong?"
"That... That lady looks familiar." Darian replied with a frown. "I’m sure I’ve seen her somewhere before, but I can’t remember her name..."

’...You have a photographic memory, yet you don’t remember?’ Soren raised a brow, then guessed the trait mustn’t be fully developed yet, or Darian had seen just a glimpse of her. But his curiosity was already piqued. ’...Well, it won’t hurt to take a look, right?’
Soren pulled out his phone, unlocked the screen, and opened the search bar. Typing in the name Shabnam Mahren, he tapped search and waited for the results to load.
’W-Whoa!’ His eyes widened slightly at the flood of headlines filling the screen.
Among the countless news articles and forum discussions, the top search result immediately caught his attention:
"The ’Lightning Queen’ Returns: Former S-Rank Hunter Shabnam Mahren Formally Announces Her Comeback After 10 Years Of Retirement!"1

chapters.title: Chapter 402: Ademary Awakened Bureau [2]
paragraphs: ’Huh?! She’s an S-rank Hunter?’ Soren’s eyes widened in surprise.
He tapped on the article and began reading. And within just ten minutes, he had absorbed a wealth of information about her and her past.

It turned out she had been a famous S-rank hunter a long time ago. Even with 6th-Circle cultivation, her overwhelming combat power allowed her to participate in 7th-Circle Gate raids and stand toe-to-toe with Pseudo Emperors and even with some early-stage Emperors.

However, around ten years ago, her husband died in an accident, and she retired to take care of her twin daughters and disappeared from public view. While some articles pointed to her husband’s death as a breaking point, others speculated that she simply wanted to focus entirely on raising her daughters.

Other pieces, however, leaned into darker rumors, claiming her husband had perished during an incident because of her, leaving her burdened with intense guilt and driving her into a life of isolation.

Soren didn’t know which info was true, but he guessed there must be some kind of story behind it. It’s because her late husband had originally been a noble from a powerful family, and he had been cast out years earlier, with his status as an unawakened being as the primary reason for his exile.
’Well, I can at least tell that she’s a remarkable woman.’

Choosing to marry an unawakened outcast from a powerful family, stepping away from her peak career to raise her daughters herself, and staying out of the spotlight for a decade spoke volumes about her loyalty and character.
’It must have been difficult-hmm?’

Before he could finish the thought, he noticed several people approaching at a fast pace and heightened his guard. Soon, a group of individuals dressed in formal attire stepped into the building, led by a stern, black-haired middle-aged man.
The moment they entered, the staff members immediately stood at attention, their voices rising in respectful unison:
"Director!"
The man merely nodded before brushing past them, walking at a hurried pace toward the inner evaluation hall.
As the doors closed behind the entourage, chatter erupted across the waiting area.
"Director? Is that... is that the famous Martial Emperor?
"Whoa! Did we just see the legend in person?!"
"I can’t believe he’s actually here today..."
Ryan and Darian were no different, as they recognized the man too.
"Senior Ryan! It really was the Martial Emperor, right?! Right?"
"Y-Yes! They called him director too, so there’s no way it’s a mistake."
"COOL!"

"..." Soren chuckled inwardly at their reactions, but it was understandable since he also knew a bit about the Martial Emperor thanks to his research last night. Having already used Eyes of Truth on them, he started reviewing their status windows.
’...He truly deserved to be called a legend.’

He muttered inwardly as he finished checking Martial Emperor’s profile. He had 9th-circle potential and was currently at the peak of the 7th circle, with a massive amount of mana, even for an Emperor.
’I think I understand why he is called Martial Emperor now, too.’

It was all because of his SSS Rank ability called Weapon Mastery. Despite sounding simple, it was incredibly powerful. Although he couldn’t learn much, its description told him that the ability allows him to master any weapon in existence pretty easily, effortlessly drawing out its ultimate potential while exponentially boosting his combat instincts and destructive output with every weapon he held.
In the hands of someone with his immense mana pool and peak 7th-Circle strength, it meant he was nearly unbeatable in close-quarters combat — a true master of all arms.
’With someone like him running things,’ Soren thought as he watched the closed doors of the evaluation hall, ’the Awakened Bureau is even more formidable than the rumors suggest.’
And the reason they came running was probably related to the twins. Their awakening must have created some kind of phenomenon, immediately catching the attention of the higher-ups.
’...Does that mean a similar scene will happen if Darian awakens?’

He mused on the thought, a faint smile touching his lips. Given Darian’s 8th-Circle potential and unique traits, an evaluation room spectacle was practically guaranteed. Well, as long as he awakened, that is.
’...Wait, does that mean only 8th- and 9th-Circle potentials attract this kind of attention?’

He hadn’t seen people react with anywhere near this level of urgency for 7th-Circle potentials. Even his own official registry had been handled with standard procedures rather than a red-carpet rush from top leadership.
Then again, the number of Awakened with S-Rank potential was relatively high compared to the tiers above them, so the selective frenzy was understandable.

Time ticked by slowly as the remaining evaluations continued. One candidate after another went inside and came back out, but neither the Director nor Shabnam and her daughters ever returned to the main waiting area.

’They must have left through a private exit or are still inside,’ Soren guessed and kept waiting. After twenty minutes, a loud chime echoed through the speakers, and their assigned numbers flashed on the digital board.
Soren turned to Darian. "Are you ready?"
Darian nodded enthusiastically, his eyes bright with excitement. "Ready!"
"Then let’s go."

Three of them made their way to the testing hall. The room was large, with high ceilings and reinforced walls covered in runes. At the center stood a circular platform, surrounded by a barrier. It was commonly known as the Awakening Platform.
A staff member met them at the entrance. "Only the applicant may enter the testing area. Guardians and companions can watch from the observation room."
Soren nodded and turned to Darian. "We’ll be right outside. Good luck."
"You can do it!" Ryan added with an encouraging smile.
"Thank you, Master Soren, Senior Ryan!" Darian gave them a quick thumbs-up and headed inside.

Soren and Ryan stepped into the observation room and watched Darian listen to the instructions, then head to the platform. He climbed the short flight of steps onto the elevated dais. He sat cross-legged at the center, took a deep breath, and closed his eyes.
A moment later, the intricate magic circle carved into the platform beneath him lit up with a radiant glow, indicating the start of the awakening test.

chapters.title: Chapter 403: Ademary Awakened Bureau [3]
paragraphs: The awakening test was a process both remarkably complex and deceptively simple.

While Soren didn’t know every technical detail or the deep magical formulas powering the apparatus, he understood the fundamental flow of how it operated. After all, he had experienced it himself a few times, though all of them ended in failure.
Anyway, the first step was the easiest, yet undoubtedly the most crucial part of the entire evaluation. It would determine whether one could awaken or not.

First, the magic circle beneath the candidate would activate, stimulating their body and soul. It would act as a catalyst, coaxing the dormant vessel, attempting to awaken the internal pathways, and drawing forth the true potential from within.

Once the initial catalyst settled, the crystal pillars would rise around the platform and begin radiating steady waves of pure, neutral mana directly into the candidate, bathing their physical frame to measure the body’s natural capacity to absorb and hold power.

The process would repeat, sending wave after wave until the body showed a reaction. If a candidate lacked talent, the neutral mana would simply pass through them without a trace. But if their dormant mana pathways could conduct it, they would catch the energy, causing the pillars to light up and confirming their capacity to hold mana and awaken their core.
’So far, everything is going smoothly...’
Through the observation glass, Soren watched as the first pulse was released.
Nothing happened.
The mana passed right through him without encountering any resistance or leaving a single trace behind.
Then came the second pulse.

Again, the neutral energy swept over the platform, attempting to stimulate any dormant mana pathways. Once more, the platform registered zero conduction, the mana slipping through Darian’s body as if he were made of air.
The lead evaluator behind the glass sighed and reached for the control console to initiate the next pulse of the sequence.
Time passed, and they kept going.

At the fifth pulse, the faintest spark of mana caught in Darian’s pathways before vanishing as quickly as it appeared. The evaluator paused, checked the readings, then shook his head and continued. The next three pulses were also unsuccessful.
Then, on the ninth pulse, another brief flicker of energy flared around Darian’s body, only to dissipate a moment later.
They kept going for five more pulses, but got no results. Soren saw the lead evaluator sigh in disappointment and announce.
"We’re applying the final pulse. If there’s no reaction after this, the test ends."
"Darian...
Ryan muttered in a tense voice, his hands pressed against the glass.

Soren clenched his fists too, feeling Darian’s intense emotions even from a distance. Though he sat as if nothing had changed, the boy was actually terrified. The panic, the desperation, and the fear of failure... Soren could see it all with perfect clarity.
’...Come on, Darian. Don’t give up. Believe in yourself.’
Soren encouraged as the final pulse flowed into Darian’s body. However, it continued to pass straight through him, just like every attempt before.
Soren’s eyes widened as he saw the mana that was about to leave Darian’s body suddenly collapse inward, pulled deep into his chest like water down a drain.
"He did it!"
He exclaimed in a low voice, and at the same time, the pillars shone brightly in a pure silver color.

Inside the observation room, the lead evaluator’s hand froze over the shutdown lever. The flatline monitors spiked without warning, the numeric readings surging upward so fast the numbers blurred on the glass.
"Override the safety limit! Keep the stream open! He’s drawing it in!"
At the man’s orders, the assistants scrambled across the control desk, rapidly keying in the override codes to unlock the mana throttles and force the transition into the ignition phase.
On the dais, the silver glow around Darian began to distort. His physical form trembled, the outlines of his arms and shoulders blurring into faint, shifting static.
"What’s happening?" Ryan muttered, staring intensely at the flickering outline.
"...Could it be... his ability?" Soren responded, never taking his eyes off Darian as he tracked the volatile spikes on the display monitor. He didn’t forget to keep an eye on his status too.
Before Ryan could answer, a loud shout broke out from the control desk.
"Space affinity!" an assistant yelled, pointing at the rapidly shifting energy signatures on his screen. "It’s space! At least grade seven!"
The whole room instantly burst into noise. Staff members leaned over consoles, shouting out rising figures as the platform readings climbed into high-tier parameters.

"Hmm?" Soren raised a brow as he sensed something wrong. The surroundings were shifting out of sync. The ground under his feet gave a weightless sensation, as though the room were dropping out from beneath him, only to slam back down with double the force. Perspective warped across his field of vision; the edges of the observation desk bent into unnatural angles, and the far wall seemed simultaneously inches away and a mile deep.
’...Is... space distorting or something?’
He turned his attention back to the platform and saw Darian’s body glitching rapidly until he vanished entirely for seconds at a time before reappearing.
’Not good!’ Sorenp glanced at Darian’s profile, his gaze scanning the changing lines of text.
Name: Darian Dervish
Race: Human
Age: 15
Status: Awakening (Core Ignition)
Rank: ? (Awakening in progress)
Mental State: Trance
Hidden Talent / Traits: Photographic Memory, Serendipity’s Fool, Uncommon Wisdom
Affinities: Space (Grade 9 - SSS Rank), Lightning (Grade 7 - S Rank)
Abilities: ? (Awakening in progress)
Potential: 9th Circle
Investment Value: MYTHIC
’Is he ok or not?’ He cursed inwardly as the status didn’t give him a clear answer. The screen flickered and updated again, but the lines that mattered most were still shrouded in uncertainty.

To make matters worse, the situation deteriorated by the second. Hair-thin fractures spiderwebbed across the glass, spreading upward like ice. Across the hall, the sheer pressure of the spatial warp bore down on the staff. Some of the weaker ones dropped to their knees, clutching their heads in pain, then collapsed against the consoles.
"Rran, stay here! I will-!"

Then, on the ninth pulse, another brief flicker of energy flared around Darian’s body, only to dissipate a moment later.
They kept going for five more pulses, but got no results.
Soren saw the lead evaluator sigh in disappointment and announce.
"We’re applying the final pulse.
If there’s no reaction after this, the test ends."
"Darian...
Ryan muttered in a tense voice, his hands pressed against the glass.
Soren clenched his fists too, feeling Darian’s intense emotions even from a distance.
Though he sat as if nothing had changed, the boy was actually terrified.
The panic, the desperation, and the fear of failure...
Soren could see it all with perfect clarity.
’...Come on, Darian.
Don’t give up.
Believe in yourself.’
Soren encouraged as the final pulse flowed into Darian’s body.
However, it continued to pass straight through him, just like every attempt before.
Soren’s eyes widened as he saw the mana that was about to leave Darian’s body suddenly collapse inward, pulled deep into his chest like water down a drain.
"He did it!"
He exclaimed in a low voice, and at the same time, the pillars shone brightly in a pure silver color.
Inside the observation room, the lead evaluator’s hand froze over the shutdown lever.
The flatline monitors spiked without warning, the numeric readings surging upward so fast the numbers blurred on the glass.
"Override the safety limit!
Keep the stream open!
He’s drawing it in!"
At the man’s orders, the assistants scrambled across the control desk, rapidly keying in the override codes to unlock the mana throttles and force the transition into the ignition phase.
On the dais, the silver glow around Darian began to distort.
His physical form trembled, the outlines of his arms and shoulders blurring into faint, shifting static.
"What’s happening?" Ryan muttered, staring intensely at the flickering outline.
"...Could it be... his ability?" Soren responded, never taking his eyes off Darian as he tracked the volatile spikes on the display monitor.
He didn’t forget to keep an eye on his status too.
Before Ryan could answer, a loud shout broke out from the control desk.
"Space affinity!" an assistant yelled, pointing at the rapidly shifting energy signatures on his screen.
"It’s space!
At least grade seven!"
The whole room instantly burst into noise.
Staff members leaned over consoles, shouting out rising figures as the platform readings climbed into high-tier parameters.
"Hmm?" Soren raised a brow as he sensed something wrong.
The surroundings were shifting out of sync.
The ground under his feet gave a weightless sensation, as though the room were dropping out from beneath him, only to slam back down with double the force.
Perspective warped across his field of vision; the edges of the observation desk bent into unnatural angles, and the far wall seemed simultaneously inches away and a mile deep.
’...Is... space distorting or something?’
He turned his attention back to the platform and saw Darian’s body glitching rapidly until he vanished entirely for seconds at a time before reappearing.
’Not good!’ Sorenp glanced at Darian’s profile, his gaze scanning the changing lines of text.
Name: Darian Dervish
Race: Human
Age: 15
Status: Awakening (Core Ignition)
Rank: ? (Awakening in progress)
Mental State: Trance
Hidden Talent / Traits: Photographic Memory, Serendipity’s Fool, Uncommon Wisdom
Affinities: Space (Grade 9 - SSS Rank), Lightning (Grade 7 - S Rank)
Abilities: ? (Awakening in progress)
Potential: 9th Circle
Investment Value: MYTHIC
’Is he ok or not?’ He cursed inwardly as the status didn’t give him a clear answer.
The screen flickered and updated again, but the lines that mattered most were still shrouded in uncertainty.
To make matters worse, the situation deteriorated by the second.
Hair-thin fractures spiderwebbed across the glass, spreading upward like ice.
Across the hall, the sheer pressure of the spatial warp bore down on the staff.
Some of the weaker ones dropped to their knees, clutching their heads in pain, then collapsed against the consoles.
"Rran, stay here!
I will-!"

paragraphs: "Ryan! Stay here, I-!"
BOOM!
A violent spatial wave detonated from the dais, and the world descended into darkness. The glass pane shattered into countless sharp shards, spraying directly toward their faces.

Soren instantly snapped his arm forward, manifesting a dense wall of ice stacked with a thick layer of reinforced mana. And yet, the flying glass cut through both defenses, tearing through the barriers as if they were made of paper.

"!" Soren grabbed Ryan by the shoulder, spun his body, and threw himself over the younger boy. Ice erupted across Soren’s body, hardening into a thick set of frost armor just as the debris slammed into him. The impact shoved him forward, the fragments digging deep into his ice shell.
Then, the chaos snapped shut.
The violent shaking ceased instantly. The ground went dead still, and the color and light returned. The crushing pressure vanished in a fraction of a second, leaving the space completely motionless.

"?" Soren frowned deeply and turned around, the frost armor sliding off his back in fragments. Across the ruined room, golden light shimmered in neat arcs, forming individual protective shields around every collapsed staff member.
In the center of the dais, a familiar tall figure stood directly behind Darian, one hand resting calmly on the boy’s back.
"Martial Emperor..."
The name slipped out of Soren’s mouth.
The man’s presence on the dais instantly suppressed whatever phenomenon was unfolding while locking down the spatial fractures that had been tearing the surroundings apart.
’No. He is using his domain.’
Soren corrected his initial thought and looked down at Ryan, who was still catching his breath on the floor.
"Are you ok?"

Ryan nodded quickly, wiping sweat from his forehead. Satisfied, Soren turned back to the broken glass frame. Together, they leaped through the shattered window and landed cleanly on the hall floor. They hurried across the cracked tiles and approached the edge of the dais.
"Is there any way we can help?" Soren asked, looking at the Martial Emperor.
The Emperor turned his gaze toward him, his expression unreadable. "...Help the head evaluator."

"Understood," Soren said, nodding without hesitation. He pivoted and went over to the man struggling to get up. Uncapping a healing potion, he fed it to him, then grabbed his arm and pulled him upright. The evaluator thanked him, turned to the console, and slammed his hand onto the controls.
The pillars roared back to life along with the barrier. Beneath Darian’s feet, the magic circle ignited once more, brighter than ever.
"Huff..." The man exhaled tiredly. "Now, as long as he forms a core, it will be over."
Soren stepped back and handed Ryan a few healing potions. They moved through the hall, helping the staff who had collapsed and handing out vials until everyone was back on their feet.
Darian stayed still in his trance state, pulling in every stream of mana to form his core. Martial Emperor stayed in contact with him, likely to keep him from glitching again.
"...Sir, do you know why that happened?" Soren asked after returning to the leader’s side. "Is it because of his ability or affinity?"

"You are his guardian, right?" The man smiled and patted Soren on the shoulder. "Congratulations. This boy is undoubtedly a once-in-a-million prodigy. His space affinity sits well above Grade 7, probably Grade 8, or with a glimmer of a chance at Grade 9. Our current technology isn’t developed enough to measure space or other abstract affinities with perfect accuracy, so we can’t tell the exact grade, but you get what I mean, right?"
"Yes." Soren nodded. "Then that phenomenon..."
"Ah yes, the phenomenon is definitely related to his ability. I think it’s a rare spatical constitution type too. We’ll know for sure once the test is over."
Soren nodded in understanding, thanked the man, then turned back toward the platform, joining the rest of the room as they silently watched the process unfold.
Time passed, and Darian finally opened his eyes, making everyone sigh in relief.
"Huh? W-What happened here?" He looked baffled as he took in his surroundings, staring at the cracked floor tiles, shattered glass panes around the hall, and the pale-faced people.
"Hmm?" As if sensing someone directly behind him, he turned and looked up. His body went rigid, eyes widening.
"M-Ma-Ma—Martial Emperor?!"
The Martial Emperor smiled faintly and tapped him gently on the shoulder. "You caused quite a commotion, boy. But I have to say, I am really impressed."
"T-Thank you?" Darian muttered, still not understanding what was happening around him.

The Martial Emperor smiled again, patted Darian’s shoulder once more, and stepped off the platform. The moment the Emperor left, Darian’s body gave out, and he collapsed onto his back, and his face went pale from exhaustion.
"Continue with the test," the Emperor said, walking over to Soren’s side.
"Yes, Director! Thank you for your help," the head evaluator replied, bowing deeply before calling out to the staff. "Everyone, return to your stations! Resume the process!"
Soren and Ryan immediately turned toward the Martial Emperor and bowed their heads.
"Thank you for stepping in, Your Excellency," Soren said.
"It is my job." The Emperor waved his hand carelessly. "But... once this is over, I would like to have a talk with you, if that’s alright."
Soren nodded. "Of course."
He knew right away that the conversation would revolve around Darian.
’Even so, it’s good for me too. Perhaps I can build a connection with the Martial Emperor through this.’

With that thought, he turned back to watch the rest of the evaluation, and with the Martial Emperor personally keeping an eye on the process, the test went smoothly. Darian slowly pushed himself back into a sitting position and continued to follow every direction he was given, even as he struggled to process everything that had just happened.
Within five minutes, the procedure finally came to an end.
The head evaluator stepped forward, looked down at his freshly updated tablet, then raised his voice to announce the official results.
"Darian Dervish! Awakening successful! Final assessment..."

As soon as the results were announced, the screen above their head also updated, displaying the full breakdown of Darian’s evaluation in glowing golden letters.
Darian stood beside Soren, completely dumbfounded. His eyes were fixed on the screen, but he didn’t seem to be reading the words. He just stared, his mouth slightly open.
"Your dream has finally come true, Darian." Soren reached over and rubbed the boy’s head. "Good job on not giving up."
Darian finally broke out of his daze. He looked at Soren and asked.
"I’m not dreaming, right, Master?"
Soren shook his head and suggested after a pause. "You can pinch yourself if you want to be sure."
Darian nodded, pinched his own cheek. "O-Ow!" He cried out loud from pinching too hard, but his face soon broke into a grin.
"It’s real! It’s actually real!" He jumped to his feet, his fists raised in the air. "Yay! I did it! I really did it!"
The trio and the surrounding staff let out light laughs at his sudden burst of energy, the earlier tension in the hall completely evaporating.
"Let’s go now," Soren said, patting his shoulder. "We have already taken up a lot of time."
Darian stopped jumping and nodded obediently, though his eyes remained wide and full of joy as he stepped into line beside him.
"Then, please follow me." The Martial Emperor smiled and led the way under the admiring gazes of the staff.

Soren thought some of them might feel jealous or envious, but he could tell that was not the case. Most of them were relieved, exhausted, or simply indifferent, while the rest even seemed happy. He guessed they must be content with their lives, happy that their nation had given rise to a new future powerhouse, or just used to seeing people like Darian awaken. Or perhaps they had seen so many over the years that it no longer surprised them.
’Yeah, they didn’t seem that much surprised by the phenomenon earlier, too.’
The Martial Emperor led them to a room on the third floor and offered them seats. Once they sat down, a staff member brought coffee for everyone.
Soren picked up his mug, took a brief sip, and looked across the table.
"I am Soren, Darian’s sponsor and guardian. First, I want to clarify that I will take full responsibility for the damages caused during his awakening earlier."

’...It was really my fault?’ Darian’s head perked up, but remembering what Soren had told him on the way about not worrying and letting him handle everything, he kept his mouth shut and lowered his gaze back to his cup.

"Don’t worry about the repair costs," the Emperor said with a smile. "The bureau handles damages caused by awakening phenomena. It’s factored into our budget. Cases like this are rare, but they do happen."
"I see..."
"More importantly, let’s talk about the boy." Martial Emperor glanced at Darian, whose ears perked up almost immediately. "What is he planning to do in the future?"
"He will be entering the Etenia Academy to study. As for his path after that, it will be up to him, but it is still too early to think about that for now."
The Martial Emperor turned his gaze to Darian and spoke again only after Darian nodded affirmatively.

"Right... I hope you manage to get into the academy. But for now, I want to talk about your abilities and your awakening." Martial Emperor was curious because even a skilled awakened’s appraisal ability couldn’t see the boy’s true abilities. "Can you tell me what you experienced during the process? Did you feel any pain, any strange sensations, or did you feel nothing at all?"
At the question, Ryan also turned toward Darian, his eyes brimming with curiosity as he waited for an answer. Soren was even more curious, since he knew exactly what abilities Darian possessed.

Darian took a moment to gather his thoughts before he began. "At first, when it started, I was really happy. I felt the foreign energy moving inside me and my body absorbing it. But then... I suddenly lost my sense of self."
He paused, looking down at the surface of his coffee as if trying to recall the exact details.

"I felt as if I was floating. Sometimes it felt like I was somewhere else entirely, or like parts of my body were missing. But strangely, I didn’t feel any pain. There was just this weird sensation and a bit of slight discomfort."
The trio nodded, having seen the phenomenon with their own eyes. They were also relieved it hadn’t been as painful as they suspected.

"Then I found myself in a dark place." Darian continued, his brows furrowing. "I couldn’t discern where I was, which direction I was facing, or even my own weight. But I could feel things passing right through me, even though I couldn’t move or do anything about it. And then, all of a sudden, I returned to reality."

"...Hmm." Martial Emperor nodded subtly, his expression thoughtful. He then turned to Soren. "I think it will be dangerous for the boy to cultivate by himself. Moreover, he mustn’t try to use his abilities or his spatial affinity at all without the guidance of a master spatial awakened."
"You mean..." Soren leaned forward, his brow narrowing. "...the phenomenon from earlier might repeat itself?"

"That’s right," the Emperor confirmed, setting his mug down on the table. "And if such a thing happens, he might end up hurting himself, the people, and the environment around him. Things will be even trickier when he tries to break through."
"...We should find him a personal teacher who is specialized in space, then, right?" Soren asked.
The Martial Emperor nodded in agreement.
"Then thank you for the advice. I will take care of it as soon as I can." Soren paused before adding. "Is there anything else we need to discuss, or can we take our leave?"
The Emperor shifted slightly, his gaze locking onto Soren. "I would like to speak with you alone for a moment, if that is alright."
Soren nodded and turned toward the rest of the group. "Ryan, take Darian outside to wait for a bit."
"Understood," Ryan replied, standing up and gesturing for Darian to follow him out the door.
Once the door clicked shut and the room fell silent, the Martial Emperor leaned back in his seat, his eyes softening.
"It’s good to see you looking well, Chef Soren."

Soren froze, genuine surprise flashing across his face before he quickly smoothed his expression and settled into steady composure. ’I should find a better disguise artifact as soon as possible, too.’

"I know about the Bagdad City incident," the Emperor continued smoothly. "I was away at the time, so I could not step in to help. I only received the full report after the Outcasts extermination mission concluded. It seems like the Teleportation Gates were blocked during the incident, making it impossible for other cities, including ours, to lend a hand in time. Thankfully, the villains couldn’t achieve their true goal. And I heard from City Lord Asad that you played quite an important role."

’...The Puppeteer was probably the one who tampered with the gates.’ Soren guessed inwardly and shook his head. "You are flattering me, Your Excellency. I did nothing worth mentioning; it was all City Lord and Commander Ervin who handled everything and deserve the praise."
"There is no need to be humble, Mr. Soren. I already know the truth." The Martial Emperor replied, a knowing smile playing on his lips. "After all, I heard it from the victims themselves."
"Before you misunderstand, I was one of the high-ranking figures who escorted the survivors back to the capital, so I learned the details entirely by accident."
"Really?" Soren narrowed his eyes at the Emperor, his expression remaining completely impassive, refusing to betray a single thought.

The Emperor chuckled softly and raised a hand. "Alright, let us just say I have a personal history with those scums. And I wanted to know the true benefactor who beat them up that good and ruined their plan, so I interrogated the captives nicely for a bit."
’...I am sure "nicely" is doing a lot of work in that sentence. But...’
"Are there other people who know the truth?"

"Probably yes, but not because of me." The Martial Emperor explained. "Those who interrogated them later in the capital would have learned the details too, and the higher-ups who reviewed the reports would know as well. To be honest, it’s no secret in certain circles. Fortunately, it hasn’t been made public. Well, not yet, at least."

Soren.

chapters.title: Chapter 406: Martial Emperor’s Offer
paragraphs: Soren fell silent at the emperor’s words.

He already knew some people would naturally discover the truth, and even though the princess and the city lord promised to keep it a secret, he never fully believed they could hold the line forever. There were simply too many individuals with greater power and status than them within the empire.

And now that his assumptions had proven true, he could only hope the news would remain buried from the public long enough for them to finish their affairs here and take their leave before the truth was revealed to the world.
’Then again, even if the empire discloses it, the outcasts might spread it themselves.’
Although they were currently on the run and hiding, they still possessed enough resources and underground connections to stir up trouble like that.
"You seem to have a lot on your mind," the Emperor said, breaking the silence as he leaned back in his seat.

Soren offered a faint smile. "I think almost everyone in the world has something on their mind. Still, I appreciate you sharing them with me. But then again... you didn’t hold me back just to talk about those, did you?"
"...Mm." Emperor’s lips curled up. "Actually, I wanted to invite you to something interesting."
"I’m all ears," Soren said, after all, hearing him out wouldn’t cost him anything.
The Emperor folded his hands on the table and met Soren’s gaze directly.
"Mr. Soren... Do you want to go on a villain hunt?"
’...A villain hunt?’ Soren raised an eyebrow. "...Is this related to the announcement His Majesty made?"
"It is," the Martial Emperor nodded. "And there will be substantial compensation and rewards depending on how well you do."

"I understand, but..." Soren gave a brief nod, though his expression remained guarded. "Why are you inviting me? I am merely a low-ranking cultivator. I am hardly capable of standing against threats on your level, Your Excellency."
"Just tell me if you’re interested," the Emperor countered, waving off the excuse. "I guarantee your safety, and you won’t be fighting Emperors or anyone above the fifth circle."
"...You mean I’ll be fighting 5th Circles?"
"That’s right. Or... are you afraid?"
Soren narrowed his eyes, ignoring the Emperor’s taunt as he began weighing the risks against the potential gains.
"When is this happening?" Soren asked. "And can I get the full details before I make my decision?"
"...Hmm. Fine." The Emperor hesitated, rubbing his chin as if making a difficult concession. "Since you are taking this seriously, I will give you the full breakdown."

He laid out the specifics without holding back. Their target was an elusive underground criminal organization operating in one of their neighboring cities. He detailed their crimes, operational structure, suspected hideouts, and the exact scope of the raid, while Soren listened attentively, taking in every word and processing the risks involved.
"So, what do you think?" the Emperor asked, leaning forward once he finished. "Do you want to participate?
Soren, whose gaze had long grown cold after learning about the villains, nodded and spoke in a chilling tone. "I will. Thank you for granting me this opportunity."

"Good." The Emperor reached into his inner coat pocket and pulled out a strange phone-like device, placing it on the table between them. "Take this. We will contact each other through it when the time comes." Soren took it and stored it in his storage after studying it a bit. "By the way, if you need any help while preparing, don’t hesitate to ask. I will do what I can to accommodate your requests. And off the record, there is no need for such stiff formality. You can simply call me Sir, or even Uncle Xolid."

Soren thought for a moment before speaking up. "Sir, I need a high-tier disguise artifact, one even you or other emperors or Sovereigns won’t be able to see through. I wonder if you could help me source one? Of course, I will pay for it in full."
"That can be arranged." Emperor Xolid nodded in understanding. "Are you free right now, or is there something else you need to take care of first?"
"I need to handle Darian’s training arrangements, and I plan to apply for a promotion," Soren replied honestly.
"A promotion?" The Emperor raised a brow. "Are you already elevating to a Senior Magic Chef? Hoho, as expected of the-"
"Ah, no," Soren cut the man off, shaking his head slightly. "I meant I want to upgrade my Hunter license."
"Huh?" The Emperor paused, momentarily dumbfounded.
"...And I am already a Senior Magic Chef," Soren added evenly.
"Ah. I see." The Emperor cleared his throat, quickly regaining his composure before leaning forward. "What is your current rank?"
"I am a C-Rank Hunter," Soren said. "I plan to apply for B-Rank."
The Emperor nodded, a slight smile returning to his face. "Alright, consider it done."
"Eh?" Soren blinked, now the one caught off guard.

"I will handle the paperwork myself," the Emperor said smoothly. "There is no need for you to waste time taking the promotion exam. If you could handle the Hollow Pair, then you’re more than qualified for B-rank."
"Is that really alright?" Soren asked, raising an eyebrow.

"I am the Director here," the Martial Emperor waved his hand dismissively. "There is nothing wrong with using proper discretion, nor are we doing anything improper. Besides... you want to keep a low profile and hide your true identity, don’t you?"
Soren fell silent and nodded gratefully. "Thank you for your consideration, Sir."
"Don’t mention it. Consider it a small token of thanks for taking care of the Hollow pair back then."
"Mm. If there’s nothing else, I will take my leave."
"Right, just leave your current Hunter license and a copy of your ID with my secretary," the Emperor said. "You can swing back by this afternoon to pick up the updated license."
Just then, a sleekly dressed man wearing thin-framed glasses knocked once and stepped into the office. Soren handed over his documents to the secretary as instructed, then turned to exit the room.
Rejoining Ryan and Darian in the hallway, Soren gestured for them to follow, and the three of them quietly made their way out of the building.
Emperor Xolid instructed his secretary what to do right after Soren left the room. "...Make sure to have it completed by lunch.

"Master, is this really necessary?" the secretary asked, adjusting his glasses as he looked down at the documents in his hand. "Issuing a direct rank advancement without the practical assessment... isn’t this against the rules?"

Martial Emperor Xolid chuckled softly without turning around. "You are so rigid sometimes, you know that? But tell me... do you remember how many of our hunters fell to the Outcasts during these past few years, especially to the Hollow pair?"
The secretary paused, his expression growing solemn. "...More than a hundred."
"Right," Xolid said, resting his hands behind his back. "And how many of them were high-ranked?"
"Nearly a third were B-Rank and A-Rank hunters, Master."
"Right." Xolid turned, his gaze sharpening. "So now, do you understand why?"
The secretary lowered his head slightly and placed Soren’s documents into a leather portfolio. "I understand now. Forgive me for doubting your judgment, Master."
"Good," Xolid said with a brief nod. "If you understand, then get to work. And again, make sure everything stays between us."
"Understood, Master. My lips are sealed." The secretary bowed his head, then paused, hesitating for a fraction of a second before speaking up again. "May I ask one more thing, Master?"
"Go on."
"Can I... also participate in the hunt?"
Xolid glanced at him, a half-smile returning to his face. "We will talk about that later. It depends on your attitude."
"Understood."
The secretary bowed once more, tucked the portfolio beneath his arm, and quickly stepped out of the room, leaving Xolid alone.
Xolid sighed as he lay back on the sofa.

Actually, there were a few things he hid from both Soren and his secretary, who also happened to be his disciple. He didn’t tell his disciple that Soren might be the one who killed the Puppeteer, the one the disciple had long wanted to kill.

First, it was still only a guess, since City Lord Asad or Commander Ervin hadn’t revealed or acknowledged it, but the pieces fit too well to ignore. Second, Xolid had no intention of recklessly stoking his disciple’s lingering obsession. Finally, it was hard to admit, but his disciple was a bit narrow-minded and hot-headed. If Soren truly was the one who eliminated the Puppeteer, letting his disciple pick an unnecessary fight over a personal grudge would only ruin the entire operation before it even began.
He could only hope the fellow would eventually mature and outgrow those flaws before they cost him something far greater. For now, though, keeping him out of the loop was the safest choice.
Or, more honestly...
He didn’t want to ruin the perfect chance to see Soren in action with his own eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 407: Darian’s Future
paragraphs: ’...’ Soren noticed that since leaving the bureau, Darian hadn’t said a single word and wore a troubled expression, staring blankly out the window. ’Hmm... I guess the reality of what happened is finally sinking in.’
Still, he decided to ask the boy himself. "Darian, is something on your mind?"
Darian looked up and couldn’t help but recall what he had heard from his senior Ryan earlier while his master Soren was inside. "Master Soren... Can I really get into the Academy?"
Soren glanced at the rearview mirror, meeting Darian’s hesitant eyes in the glass.
"If you train hard enough, you can," he stated calmly.
"But..." Darian bit his lower lip, shifting nervously in his seat. "What if I end up hurting someone? Maybe it’s better if I just... give-"
"Darian," Soren interrupted, his voice firm as he caught the boy’s gaze once more. "Are you saying you want to give up?"
"..." Darian said nothing, but the silence was an answer in itself.

"I think you misunderstood what the Martial Emperor said." Soren continued. "Let me simplify his words then: Darian, as long as you work under a competent teacher, train hard, and be careful, everything will be fine."
He paused briefly, letting the message sink in before continuing.
"If you throw in the towel now, you aren’t just running away from the risk. You are throwing away your dream and your entire future."

"Doing nothing doesn’t guarantee safety either. If left unchecked, your ability could spiral out of control on its own, causing far greater damage than you can imagine. So isn’t it better to pursue your path while learning to master your power, ensuring you never hurt others, including yourself?"

Soren fell silent, allowing the words to settle between them as the vehicle rolled smoothly along the avenue. He did not press the boy for an immediate response, knowing Darian needed space to process the reality of his situation.

"..." Sitting in the passenger seat, Ryan observed the exchange without uttering a word. He found himself agreeing with every point Soren made, his admiration for his senior deepening even further along the way. ’Brother Soren knows exactly when to offer encouragement and when to deliver a cold dose of reality.’

Yet Ryan also understood why Darian hesitated. Even though the boy usually came across as lively, determined, and optimistic, he was still young and suddenly carrying a burden far beyond his years. That’s why fear of his own strength was natural. Even Ryan’s former self would have felt the same.
Perhaps this pivotal moment was precisely the opportunity Darian needed to face his reality, grow beyond his self-doubt, and take ownership of his future.
Speaking of the future, Ryan recalled the advice and also the task Soren had given him.

Soren had told him to start building connections and gathering trustworthy people he could truly rely on. He explained they wouldn’t always be together, and the threats they would eventually face probably couldn’t be handled by the three of them alone. The more reliable allies they had, the better their chances of survival. Soren had even assured him not to worry about money or resources, promising to supply everything as long as Ryan found talented individuals with solid character.
Fortunately, the new semester at the academy was starting soon. Perhaps he could find people like that among his classmates, or even in other departments.

Ryan fell silent, his gaze drifting toward the passing scenery as memories of his previous academy surfaced. Back then, despite being outgoing and genuinely friendly, nobody wanted to associate with him simply because he was the weakest.

Now, the situation had completely flipped. He possessed far greater strength, yet his personality and social habits had changed drastically along the way. Looking down at his own hands, Ryan couldn’t help wondering if he could actually pull it off.
’...No, I have to keep trying until I make it work,’ Ryan resolved, clenching his fingers slightly against his knee. ’Besides, don’t I already have two targets?’

He glanced over his shoulder at the first target, Darian. The boy seemed to have finally reached a decision, the lingering hesitation fading from his eyes as his posture straightened in the back seat. Having already seen Darian’s potential and character firsthand, Ryan knew bringing him into the fold would only be a matter of time and steady guidance.

As for the second target, Ryan knew he’d meet them soon enough. The only thing to worry about was how to treat them. ’Should I call her Sister since I call Brother Soren Brother? No, she hasn’t recovered her memories yet, so I should start as friends, or like Darian, as Senior and Junior.’
He nodded inwardly, and soon after, Darian spoke.
"Master Soren," Darian said, lifting his head to meet Soren’s eyes in the rearview mirror. "I’m sorry for saying such foolish things earlier. And thank you for knocking some sense into me."
He raised his hand, clenching his fingers tightly into a fist against his chest as resolve settled across his features.
"I swear I’ll master my abilities. I’ll work harder than anyone, grow stronger, and definitely make it into the academy. I’ll prove myself and one day, I’ll repay everything you have done for me."
Soren’s lips curved into a faint, genuine smile as he caught Darian’s determined gaze in the rearview mirror.
"Good. That is the kind of spirit I wanted to see," Soren said, his tone approving yet grounded. "Just remember not to push yourself too hard and break yourself in the process."
Darian blinked, then nodded firmly, his shoulders relaxing as the tension finally left him. "Understood, Master Soren."
"Hmm." Soren smiled and paused for a moment before speaking. "By the way, should we celebrate your awakening together first? Or do you wanna celebrate it with your family?"
"C-Celebrate?" Darian raised a brow in confusion.

"Of course," Ryan chimed in, turning slightly in his seat with an encouraging nod. "Awakening is a huge occasion. You should at least let your parents know, or better yet, prepare a surprise for them."
"Oh, I agree!"

"Yeah, picking up some gifts for his family is a great idea too," Ryan added.
"U-Uh..." Darian stammered, momentarily overwhelmed by their sudden enthusiasm. He had been so wrapped up in his fears and worries over his awakening that celebrating hadn’t even crossed his mind.
Seeing how much thought they put into both him and his family, though, warmed his chest instantly. He stopped fidgeting in his seat, the last trace of hesitation melting away into a bright smile.
"Yes! Let’s celebrate it together at our house!"
"Great, it’s settled then." Soren smiled. "Let’s head to a market. Darian, do you know any nice place?"
"Yes, Master Soren! We should go to the Great Ademary Bazaar! You can find anything there."
"Great Ademary Bazaar it is then."

True to its name, the marketplace was massive, stretching across several city blocks with towering arched entrances and bustling open-air avenues. Inside, crowds of ordinary citizens and Awakened mingled seamlessly, weaving between rows of vibrant stalls and modern storefronts.

The bazaar was divided into distinct, lively districts — everything from tailored garments and exotic spices to the latest personal technology and training gear. With Darian eagerly taking the lead as their local guide, the trio set off through the crowd.

The woman drew in a breath, her expression turning serious. "Actually, we have been hiding something from you... Something really important."
The girl stiffened for a moment, her fingers tightening around the glass before she set it aside. "What do you mean, Mother? Why would you hide anything from me?"
"We couldn’t tell you earlier because we feared it might hurt you deeply," the woman explained, her voice gentle yet measured.
The girl frowned slightly, studying her mother’s face. "Why are you deciding to tell me now, then?"

The woman hesitated, looking torn between keeping her silence and speaking the truth, before letting out a slow sigh. "It’s for the exact same reason. We didn’t want to hurt you before by bringing it up, but the situation has changed now, and we have no choice left but to tell you."
The girl gulped slightly, leaning forward across the table. "Please, tell me, Mother. What is this secret?"
The woman held her daughter’s gaze and steadied her voice. "The truth is... you have... no, you had another older brother.
The girl’s eyes widened in shock at her mother’s words. "W-What do you mean?"
"..." Instead of answering directly, the woman looked at her daughter with a sudden softness. "Are you still having nightmares, sweetie?"
The girl froze for a second before giving a weak, reluctant nod.

"Haha." A mix of sorrow and anger flashed across the woman’s face amid the hollow laugh. Her fingers tightened on the edge of the table as she muttered under her breath, "That bastard really isn’t human. Even though she lost her memories, she still can’t escape the trauma he left behind."

Being an Awakened, the girl easily caught every word. Her brows drew together as she inquired once more. "Mother, what do you mean by that? What trauma are you talking about? Please, tell me so I can understand."

"Don’t worry, I will, sweetie," the woman replied, offering a brief, comforting smile before her expression turned cold once more. "Actually, I had another child before you. A child I wish I had never given birth to..."
"Mother..." the girl murmured, startled by the raw venom in her voice.

"Ahah, sorry," the woman said, forcing a tight smile as she composed herself. "Anyway, I fell terribly ill after giving birth to him and had to remain bedridden for years before recovering. Then, when I gave birth to you, my condition relapsed, leaving me unable to care for you properly. Because of that, you grew up close to him. But... he... he turned out to be a truly awful child."

The woman’s jaw tightened as she continued, her voice dropping into a bitter cadence. "We found out too late, but it turns out that he bullied you from a very young age. He beat you whenever nobody was around to intervene, mocking and discriminating against you simply because your hair was different."
The girl instinctively reached up to touch a strand of her crimson hair, her breath hitching slightly as her mother went on.

"As if his own cruelty wasn’t enough, he was twisted enough to manipulate the other children in the family. He used his position to turn your cousins and peers against you, forcing them to isolate and torment you alongside him."

chapters.title: Chapter 409: Painted in Red
paragraphs: Nura stared at her mother in stunned silence, her fingers trembling slightly against the edge of the table as she tried to process the words.
Seeing the shock on her daughter’s face, the woman reached across and covered Nura’s hand with her own, speaking calmly, though regret still lingered in her voice.

"He was cunning enough to manipulate you into keeping quiet, too. He twisted your mind so you wouldn’t tell anyone about the discrimination or the bullying. Worse than that, he poisoned your young mind with guilt, convincing you that my illness was entirely your fault. He made you believe that I was suffering because of you, using that lie to trap you into obedience and force you to swallow every bruise and insult in silence, when in reality, he was the sole reason my health had deteriorated so badly in the first place."
The woman’s gaze hardened as her fury surfaced once more.

"Unfortunately, our father and I only discovered the truth far too late. By the time we finally uncovered everything he had done, the damage was already severe. However, we made sure he was punished accordingly for his cruelty, and it took us years of constant care and effort just to help you recover from the mental scars he left behind."
"..." Nura sat frozen in her chair, her mind going completely blank as the weight of her mother’s confession settled over her.

’W-Was I mistaken all this time?’ she thought, her gaze shifting to the crimson strands framing her mother’s face. ’Could it be... she dyed her hair red just so I wouldn’t feel alone? Did she stop calling me ’my little star’ because she was afraid it might bring back those terrible memories? Did I not feel close with her because of that? That I feared I made her sick? Was I imagining things and ended up suspecting my own parents? Why am I so-urgh!’
Before she could piece the thoughts together, a sudden pain pierced her temples.
"Urgh!"
Fragments of suppressed memories came crashing down all at once.
A tall figure with a blurred face stood over her, raising a hand to strike her down.
"Argh! I-It hurts! B-Brother, please, stop it!"
"No, this is what you deserve."
Another painful strike.
"Argh!"
"You guys, why are you staying still? Did you not want to join?"
"W-We will!"
"T-Take this!"
"Y-Yeah, look at that weird red hair! You’re a freak!"
"S-Stop crying already, you brought this on yourself!"
"Haha! Good! Good!"
Mocking laughter echoed in her ears, ridiculing the color of her hair, followed by a venomous voice whispering that her mother’s suffering was entirely her fault.
"...N-Nura! Sweetie!

Her mother’s panicked voice cut through the haze. Gasping for air, Nura drew in ragged, shaky breaths as the restaurant slowly came back into focus. Beads of cold sweat rolled down her forehead as she sat hunched forward, her fingers clutching tightly at the sides of her throbbing head.
"W-What happened?! Sweetie, are you ok?"

Her mother immediately slid into the booth beside her, wrapping her arms around Nura and pulling her into a tight embrace. "It’s okay, I’m right here," she murmured urgently, gently rubbing the back of Nura’s head and stroking her hair to soothe her trembling.
The sudden commotion drew curious glances from nearby diners, and a waiter hurried over to their booth with a concerned expression.
"Excuse me, ma’am, is everything alright? Should I call for medical assistance?"

"No, she’s fine, thank you," the woman replied smoothly, keeping one arm securely around her daughter while offering the staff member a composed smile. "Could you please bring us a damp towel and some cold water?"
"Right away, ma’am."
As the waiter stepped away, Nura buried her face against her mother’s shoulder, tears finally spilling down her cheeks as she clutched the fabric of her mother’s blouse.
"I-I’m sorry, Mother," Nura choked out between sobs, her voice raw with guilt. "I doubted you so much... I’m an awful child... Hick... Hick..."
A strange glint passed through her mother’s eyes as she looked down at the weeping girl, though her tone remained entirely warm and comforting.
"Shh, don’t say that," she whispered softly, continuing to stroke Nura’s hair. "It’s okay, sweetie. Everything is okay now. Don’t blame yourself."
"Hick... Hick..."
"There, there..."
Moments later, the waiter returned, quietly setting a glass of cold water and a neatly folded damp towel on the edge of the table before bowing slightly and taking his leave.

Nura remained buried in her mother’s embrace, her shoulders shaking as she cried for several minutes. Gradually, the tight grip she had on her mother’s blouse loosened, and her ragged sobs faded into soft, shaky breaths as she finally began to calm down.

Once Nura’s trembling subsided, her mother gently eased back just enough to reach for the glass on the table. Holding it up to Nura’s lips, she helped her take a few slow sips of the cold water. Afterward, she picked up the damp towel and carefully wiped away the sweat from Nura’s forehead and the tear tracks staining her cheeks, finishing by gently cleaning her trembling hands.
"Sweetie, have you calmed down now?"
Nura exhaled and gave a small nod.
Her mother smiled warmly, smoothing down a stray lock of Nura’s crimson hair. "Good. Then let’s leave and continue our conversation at my place; what do you say?"
Nura nodded obediently, her lingering doubts giving way to deep trust.
"Good girl~.

Raising a hand, she signaled the nearby waiter for the check. When it arrived, she settled the bill swiftly with a generous tip, then helped Nura stand. With a protective arm around her daughter’s shoulders, she guided Nura out of the restaurant, got into their car, and headed straight toward her place.
After they arrived at the hotel suite, they sat side by side on the sofa. Her mother turned to her and placed a hand on Nura’s knee.
"Sweetie, if it’s alright to ask, what did you mean earlier by saying you doubted us? Did we... do something to upset you? If so, then I sincerely-"
"N-No, no, not at all!" Nura hurriedly shook her head.

"I... I said it because..." She hesitated for a moment, her fingers twisting together in her lap before she finally spoke. "Actually, I noticed your real hair color was different, and you didn’t call me the same way you did in my childhood. So I thought... I thought you weren’t my real mother," she finished in a low voice, bowing her head in guilt.

Because she was staring down at her hands, Nura missed the way her mother’s eyes widened in shock. For a few seconds, the woman’s expression turned strange and cold. She soon forced herself to smile again, but could barely hold it.
"Mother, please forgive me," Nura pleaded, her voice trembling. "No, please punish me!"
Silence fell over the room.

Nura kept her head bowed, bracing herself for whatever punishment might follow. It would be fine even if her mother hit her, scolded her, or cursed at her. After all, she truly had been awful to doubt her own parents over something so foolish. Yet, as the seconds ticked by, the expected pain or harsh words never came.
"M-Mother?"
She slowly raised her head, fearing she might see anger or disgust staring back at her. Instead, her mother’s gaze was filled only with warmth.
"...Silly girl," her mother said with a kind smile, wrapping her arms around Nura to pull her into a hug. "Why would I punish you?"
Nura fell silent, leaning into the embrace for a moment before pulling back slightly to look at her mother and ask hesitantly. "Mother... Are you not upset or mad at me...?"

Her mother offered a gentle smile, raising a hand to tuck a strand of red hair behind Nura’s ear. "I am upset, sweetie, but not at you. I’m upset with myself for ever letting those doubts take root in your heart in the first place."
"Mother..."

"I’m also mad, but again, not at you. I’m furious at the one responsible for driving you into such a state, and mad at myself for failing to explain everything to you sooner so you wouldn’t have had to carry all of this alone."
"..." Nura lowered her gaze, her fingers tightening around the fabric of her mother’s sleeve. "I’m still sorry, Mother. I... I shouldn’t have ever questioned you."

Her mother let out a light chuckle, giving Nura’s shoulders an affectionate squeeze. "Honestly, this is a good thing too. It means our sweet Nura is really smart and doesn’t blindly trust everything she sees at face value. Hehe."
Nura blinked up at her, caught off guard by the praise.

Gradually, the playful warmth faded from her mother’s face, replaced by a serious expression as she met Nura’s eyes. "Listen, sweetie. This cautiousness of yours is going to be very useful in the future, because what I’m about to tell you is directly related to your former older brother."
"Former?" Nura raised a brow in confusion. "Is he... already dead?"
"No," her mother said, shaking her head. "But I wish he were."

chapters.title: Chapter 411: A Coincidence?
paragraphs: The sharp exclamation came from Soren, his usual calm composure breaking as he stopped dead in his tracks on the cobblestone alley.
Darian blinked in surprise and turned back toward him. "Huh? Do you know Grandma too, Master?"
Soren took a breath, forcing his expression back into something neutral before slowly shaking his head. "No, I have never met her. However, I think I might have an idea of who she is."
Inwardly, however, his mind was still reeling from the sudden shock.
’Is this just a coincidence?’
’Could she really be the exact person I have been looking for?’
After all this time of tireless searching without a single solid lead, the thought that he might have stumbled right onto her doorstep like this felt almost unreal.

Still, jumping to conclusions would only lead to disappointment. To be completely sure, Soren decided he needed to ask Darian a few questions about her first. "Darian, can you tell me about her? Is she an awakened too, or an ordinary person?"

Darian scratched his cheek, thinking it over for a moment before shaking his head. "Honestly, I have no idea if she is awakened or just an ordinary person. I have never seen her use any kind of power."

He paused, a fond smile crossing his face as they resumed walking down the shaded clay alley. "What I do know is that she is really, really smart. I learned a lot from her growing up, after all. She also has a habit of saying these deep, cryptic things that are pretty hard to wrap your head around sometimes."

Darian glanced upward as if trying to recall her exact words, then cleared his throat to imitate her tone. "She once told me, ’A human life is just a single thread woven in the dark; you never see the pattern until the loom stops.’ And another time, when I was worrying about what would happen to me in the future, that if I could really awaken, she just smiled and said, ’Tomorrow is already written in the footsteps you refuse to take today.’"
Ryan let out a low groan and rubbed his temples. "Yeah, I can see why that gave you a headache.
Soren, however, felt his heart skip a beat as those words settled in his mind. ’...I feel like this is not a coincidence at all...’
The name, the seclusion in a secluded district, and now that distinct, unsettling way of speaking Zura told him about everything aligned too closely to be dismissed as mere coincidence.
"What else, Darian? Does she ever receive strange visitors, or have anything unusual about her?"

Darian tapped his chin as they turned onto an even narrower lane where the afternoon shadows stretched long across the uneven stones. "Strange visitors? Now that you mention it, sometimes people I have never seen before come by to ask her for advice, though she turns almost all of them away at the gate. And as for anything unusual about her..."

He hesitated for a second, lowering his voice slightly as if sharing an old childhood secret. "Even though she looks old, she never seems to get sick or tire out easily. Oh, and there is one more thing: she always knows when someone is coming before they even knock on her door. When I was a kid, I thought she just had really good ears, but looking back, it was kind of strange."
Ryan raised an eyebrow. "Sounds less like a neighborhood grandma and more like some kind of hidden hermit master."
Soren didn’t answer Ryan’s joke. His jaw tightened subtly as every single detail Darian listed matched the fragments Zura and Ethea had told him about.
"...Oh, we are already here," Darian said, coming to a stop in front of a shabby yet sturdy-looking wooden gate.
Stepping up to the threshold, Darian raised a hand to knock on the worn wood. Before his knuckles could even make contact, an elderly voice drifted out from the courtyard beyond.
"Come in."

Darian paused, his hand hovering in the air. He turned back toward Soren and Ryan with a distinct ’I told you’ expression, eyebrows raised. Letting out a small chuckle, he pushed open the door and stepped through the threshold.

Entering the courtyard, they found themselves in a space that felt much older than the surrounding city. Dust motes danced in the slanted afternoon light, and the air smelled faintly of dried herbs, ink, and wool. At the far end of the courtyard, an old woman sat cross-legged on a low platform covered in worn kilims. She wore a traditional headscarf covering her head, her fingers moving with rhythmic precision as she worked on stitching a vibrant pattern into a small carpet stretched across a loom.
She paused, raised her head, and turned toward them.
"Grandma!" Darian called out loudly, waving cheerfully as he led the other two forward. "I brought the guests I told you about!"

The woman remained silent, the deep creases of her weathered face showing the weight of countless years. Yet, for all the frailty of her aged frame, her eyes held a sharpness that belied her appearance. Her gaze was unsettling: one iris split between gray and brown, the other entirely gray, as if two different people looked out from the same face.

She turned that striking gaze first toward Ryan, studying him for a few seconds before shifting her focus onto Soren. When their eyes met, her wrinkled features softened into an indescribable smile, which sent a shiver down Soren’s spine.
"Young man, it is rude to peek at other people’s secrets without permission, you know."
Soren, who had habitually used Eyes of Truth, hurriedly canceled it and bowed to her. "I apologize for my rudeness, Senior."
Beside him, Ryan and Darian exchanged baffled glances, unsure what Soren was apologizing for or why he had suddenly adopted such formal manners.
The old woman chuckled softly, leaning back slightly on her cushions as her mismatched eyes glinted with amusement.
"Alright," she said, waving a frail hand dismissively. "Since you helped out little Darian, I won’t hold it against you."
"Thank you for your generosity, Senior!"

chapters.title: Chapter 412: Grandma Kanie
paragraphs: When Eyes of Truth activated, Soren saw something he had never expected. Beneath the old woman’s frail frame, immense power lay coiled within her vessel like a sleeping serpent, masked by decades of wrinkles and apparent weakness. Deeper still, within her soul, lurked something even greater: a powerful presence, gentle on the surface yet utterly domineering in its depth. It was the kind of overwhelming force that could snuff out his life in a single move if she ever chose to unleash it.

That overwhelming realization, paired with the embarrassment of being caught red-handed peering into the depths of an existence far beyond his own, was why he had immediately dropped his gaze, bowed deeply, and apologized without a second’s hesitation.
Fortunately, the old woman showed him mercy and let the matter drop, though he still couldn’t shake the feeling that she had seen right through him, too.
"..." Darian tilted his head, looking back and forth between the two with a puzzled frown. "What are you talking about, Grandma? Master? Why can’t I understand any of this?"

The old woman chuckled softly, her mismatched eyes crinkling with warmth as she looked at him. "You are still a little young to understand these things, little Darian, though you will figure it out in time. Anyway, congratulations on your awakening. I am sure you must be very happy now."
"Ah, right!" Darian beamed, his face lighting up before he suddenly froze mid-grin and blinked in confusion. "Wait... you already know?"
His shoulders slumped slightly as he muttered quietly. "I really can’t surprise you anymore, huh..."
Beside him, Ryan raised a brow and glanced between the boy and the elderly woman. ’Shouldn’t you be more surprised about how she knew in the first place?’
"Silly boy," the old woman chuckled helplessly and asked in a meaningful tone. "You didn’t come all this way just to tell me you awakened, right?"

Darian snapped out of his daze and nodded quickly. Stepping aside slightly, he gestured toward Soren. "Right! Grandma, this is my master, Soren. He is the one who helped me awaken, and he is going to help me train so I can get into the Etenia Academy."
He then shifted his gesture toward the man standing beside Soren. "And this is Senior Ryan, a close acquaintance of ours."
Turning back to Soren and Ryan, Darian added cheerfully, "As I mentioned on the way here, this is Grandma."
Soren and Ryan both inclined their heads, offering another polite bow and greeting.
The old woman gave an approving nod, gesturing toward the low cushioned seating arranged near the wooden platform. "Come, take a seat. There is no need to stand around in the doorway."
Stepping onto the worn kilims, the three of them settled down onto the cushions, kneeling comfortably around the table.

The old woman folded her hands in her lap and turned her attention back to Darian. "Now then," she said gently, "tell me what else happened. You look as though you have been carrying quite a bit on your mind."
Darian let out a small sigh, his shoulders dropping slightly as he nodded. "I really can’t hide anything from you, Grandma."

Taking a breath, he began to recount the full story. He told her about the moment of his awakening, the incident he caused, the people he met, and the doubts that had followed after, how he had questioned whether he was truly capable of walking this path or reaching his goals. Then, his tone brightened as he described how Soren had stepped in, cutting through his hesitation and showing him a clear path forward when he had been lost in uncertainty.
Throughout the entire explanation, the old woman listened in silence, only offering an occasional nod as she took in every word.
"...Finally, recalling your words about bringing my benefactor, I brought them here." Darian finished, resting his hands on his knees.

An amiable smile spread across the woman’s weathered face. "Doubt is simply the shadow cast when you stand before a door you have never opened," she said softly while throwing him a peach he had been eyeing for some time. "You have already stepped across the threshold and passed your first hurdle, so walk forward without looking back."
"...Understood, Grandma!" Darian exclaimed as he caught the peach, though how much of her cryptic wisdom actually sank in remained anyone’s guess, as he immediately took a big bite.
She then shifted her gaze toward Soren, inclining her head slightly in a gesture of genuine gratitude. "Thank you again, young man, for guiding little Darian when he needed it most.
Soren gave a subtle nod, keeping his tone composed. "You give me too much credit, Senior. To be honest, I did it for myself as well."
The old woman nodded slowly, showing neither surprise nor disapproval. "I know. Every path crosses another for a reason, and helping someone else often clears the stones from our own road."

Her expression softened as she glanced briefly toward Darian, who was happily munching on his peach, before looking back at Soren. "Nevertheless, I will leave him in your hands. As you can see and already know, he is a bit silly and often acts before he thinks, but his heart is true, and he will be a loyal disciple if you guide him well."
Soren gave a firm nod. "I will do my best, Senior."

The old woman smiled slightly, then turned her attention to Darian. "Little Darian, why don’t you go with your senior and fetch a bucket of water from the well? Some fresh tea would be nice for our guests."
"On it, Grandma!" Darian nodded eagerly. Before standing up, he grabbed two more peaches from the tray on the table and tossed one to Ryan. "Come on, Senior Ryan, let’s go!"
