chapters.title: Chapter 413: Grandma Kanie’s Advice
paragraphs: ’She already knows what I’m here for.’ Soren’s heart rate accelerated at her words. ’And she knows about them too.’

He kept his outward expression composed, though his mind raced to process the weight of her offer. A figure of her unfathomable depth was willingly extending a lifeline, yet the condition attached was razor-sharp.
She could help only one of them.
Swallowing the dryness in his throat, Soren met her steady gaze and inclined his head slightly. "May I ask why only one, Senior?"
The old woman let out a soft sigh, her gaze drifting briefly toward the open sky above the courtyard before returning to Soren.

"Everything in this world carries a price, young man, and the heavier the fate, the steeper the toll," she said, folding her hands neatly over her lap. "Meddling with the threads of two souls bound to such turbulent destinies would bring down a backlash even I have no wish to bear in my old age."

"..." Soren listened silently. A woman of her power didn’t need to make idle threats or exaggerate consequences. If she said the backlash would be severe, it would be severe. He was just confused about how restoring lost memories could be tied so directly to fate, let alone provoke a backlash strong enough to make even someone like her hesitate.

"To sever one knot is an act of charity. Two is a debt that would cost far more than you realize." She paused and, as if reading his mind, added. "Memories are rarely sealed away without reason. Sometimes, forgetting is the only thing keeping a soul from tearing itself apart, or drawing the gaze of things best left undisturbed."

Soren’s brow furrowed slightly. He had considered the difficulty of breaking whatever seal or trauma held Ethea and Nura’s pasts captive, yet he had never viewed their amnesia as a protective barrier tied to their very destinies.
’No... She is probably only talking about Ethea since Nura isn’t involved with bigshots like her. Or... is she?’
Could the person who altered her memories be some kind of powerhouse too?
"Then... if I choose one," Soren asked carefully, keeping his voice steady, "what happens to the other?"

The old woman met his eyes without blinking. "She remains as she is, walking her current path in the dark. Until she either uncovers the truth on her own, or the weight of her past finally catches up to her."

Soren nodded slowly in understanding and asked. "Can you give me some time to think it over?" Choosing between Ethea and Nura was something he could never decide impulsively on the spot. "And when I have made my decision, how should I contact you? Should I just come directly here or...?"

"Just come here," she said simply, waving a hand as if the matter required no further complication. "When you are ready, bring the one you have chosen along with you. Until then, focus on training little Darian and keep your wits about you. Whatever you decide, make sure you are prepared to stand by it once their memories return.
"I understand." Soren inclined his head in acknowledgment.

Just as he was about to ask something else, the old woman raised a finger, her tone shifting to something slightly more casual, though her gaze remained sharp. "One more thing before those two return."
Soren paused, giving her his full attention.

"From what I can tell, you aren’t utilizing your power very well," she remarked candidly. "It might be because you have no master to guide you, or simply because there are still too many things in this world you haven’t learned yet, but you are treating what you hold like a blunt tool. You probably think you had nothing to do with little Darian’s awakening, yet if it weren’t for you and the unconscious use of your power, he wouldn’t have awakened at all."

Soren’s eyes widened in genuine shock. He had never breathed a word of his ability to anyone, yet she had seen straight through it, and from the way she spoke, she clearly understood aspects of how his power worked that even he himself hadn’t realized.

"True value only grows when you know where to place it, and knowing when to commit your resources to the right people at the right time makes all the difference," she continued smoothly, seemingly unfazed by his reaction. "At the very least, you seem to grasp that much on instinct, and you are already heading in the right direction. So pay closer attention to how you use what you have, and stop leaving your potential to chance."

Soren sat motionless as her words sank in. If his unconscious influence alone had been enough to trigger Darian’s awakening, then he had barely scratched the surface of what his authority could actually accomplish. He had been focusing purely on the surface mechanics of what he could give and receive, completely overlooking the deeper resonance the authority held when directed toward the right individuals or perhaps even places and events. Clearly, he needed to study his power far more thoroughly than he had been.

’Come to think of it, I always thought I had to be sincere and need to give something tangible just to trigger a return. Perhaps this idea was holding me back all along?’ Soren mused silently, piecing the fragments together. ’However... how did I actually influence Darian’s awakening? Could it be... because I genuinely believed he would awaken? Or because I was encouraging him at the time? ...Is my authority really tied to my own intent and desires? Hmm... Looking back, similar moments might have already happened a few times without me even noticing.’

Suddenly, several scattered observations from his past interactions clicked into place. His gaze unfocused as he entered a brief trance, his mind rapidly tracing the subtle threads of connection he had unknowingly formed with those around him. A faint ripple stirred within his core before settling back down, leaving his perception noticeably sharper than before.
A moment later, the haze cleared from Soren’s eyes. He exhaled slowly, gave a respectful nod, and looked back at the old woman. "Thank you for the guidance, Senior. I will take your words to heart."
"All I did was point toward the door," she replied. "You were the one who noticed the key was already in your hand."

’Her way of speaking reminds me of a certain someone.’ Feeling a little déjà vu, Soren absorbed the remark, letting the last remnants of that brief clarity settle firmly in his mind. Realizing she would say no more on the matter, he steered the conversation back to the matter at hand. "Regarding your assistance, Senior. Aside from bringing the one I choose, is there anything I need to do or prepare beforehand for your help? And what about the payment?
She opened her mouth to reply, but the sound of footsteps approaching from the back of the courtyard cut her off.
"We’re back!" Darian’s voice rang out cheerfully as he and Ryan stepped back into view, the boy carefully lugging a bucket brimming with fresh water while Ryan trailed a step behind.

Grandma Kanie smoothly swallowed whatever she had been about to say, her expression shifting back to that of an ordinary, unhurried host. "Set the bucket down there, little one, pour some water into the teapot, and set it over the embers."

"Don’t worry, Grandma! I haven’t forgotten how to handle things around here!" Darian nodded eagerly and hurried over to do as he was told. Meanwhile, the old woman rose from her seat and stepped inside her house, returning a moment later carrying a wooden tray arranged with sweets, dried fruits, and freshly baked bread.
Seeing her go through the trouble, Soren immediately raised a hand in polite refusal. "You really didn’t have to go to all this trouble, Senior."
She simply shook her head and set the tray down between them. "It is tradition to properly welcome guests under one’s roof. Eat up while the water heats, and save your politeness for next time."
Seeing that she would not take no for an answer, Soren conceded and helped her arrange the plates across the table. Just then, a sudden thought crossed Soren’s mind, and he glanced back toward her.
"Actually, Senior, since you went through the effort of hosting us, would you mind if I cooked a proper meal for everyone?"

Grandma Kanie froze for a heartbeat, staring at him before the corners of her lips curled up into a knowing smile. "Already looking to put your new realization to the test, are you? Go right ahead, then. Let us see what kind of meal you can put together."
Grandma Kanie paused and stared at him for a moment before the corners of her lips curled upward. "You are already thinking of ’helping,’ huh?"
Soren smiled faintly and gave a slight shrug. "That too, yes. But I also want to show my gratitude somehow for everything you have shared with me today."
She let out a soft sigh, waving a hand in concession. "Alright then, go ahead. Just keep it light."
